function: Precoding for multi-satellite cooperative downlink: a dense Transformer network maps statistical CSI to auxiliary variables of a closed-form WMMSE-type precoder, replacing the iterative algorithm (pp. 6–9).
system: S = 5 cooperating LEO satellites (600 km), each with a 10×10 UPA, serving 12–48 single-antenna users; OFDM downlink, 2 GHz, 20 MHz; no RIS (pp. 3, 10).
method: Supervised dense Transformer network (tensor-equivariant, dynamic-tanh, L = 3, D = 32) trained with a scale-invariant NMSE loss against Ā and ū labels, Adam (pp. 7–10).
data_channel: QuaDRiGa 'NTN Urban LOS' parameters aligned with 3GPP specifications (TR 38.811 cited); 5000 samples (4500 training, 500 validation, 50 test), random regions of a Walker-Delta constellation (pp. 9–10).
test_conditions: Trained at S = 5, K = 48, random power 20–50 dBm; tested with S = 3–11 and K = 12–48 (Figs. 9–10, p. 11); one QuaDRiGa scenario only.
baselines: Non-learned: single-satellite MMSE and WMMSE (SS-M, SS-WM), multi-satellite MS-SepWM, MS-JoWM, and the proposed optimization MS-JoCDWM; no other learned precoder compared (p. 10).
metrics: Average sum rate (bits/channel use) versus transmit power, κ, phase-error variance, satellites, and users; convergence; complexity order and CPU running time (pp. 10–12).
complexity: Table II (p. 12): orders such as O(NT³KS³ + LD(K²+S²)) for the DL precoder; parameters O(D²) (p. 9); CPU running time, Fig. 12 (pp. 11–12).
q1_support: p. 9: "We use the QuaDRiGa channel simulator to generate the scenario and radio channel parameters" (NTN Urban LOS scenario), which "is aligned with the channel model considered in this work and the Third Generation Partnership Project specifications [3], [46]"; [3] is TR 38.811.
q2_support: p. 10: "The network trained under the scenario with S = 5 and K = 48 can be deployed across a wide range of S and K values"; Figs. 9–10 (p. 11) test S = 3–11 and K = 12–48.
q3_support: p. 10: "The proposed DL-based method for CDWMMSE in Section IV with L = 3 and D = 32" is the only learned scheme; the other five (SS-M, SS-WM, MS-SepWM, MS-JoWM, MS-JoCDWM) are optimization-based, and the earlier DL precoders cited on p. 2 are not compared.
q4_support: p. 12: "TABLE II: Computational Complexity of Precoding Schemes" gives O(NT³KS³ + LD(K²+S²)) for MS-JoCDWM-DL; p. 11: "Fig. 12 compares the running time of several methods" on a CPU.
q5_support: p. 9: "The dataset comprises 5000 samples", generated by the authors with the QuaDRiGa simulator; no link to code or data of the proposed method is given, and the only link (reference [47]) is the QuaDRiGa repository.
notes: The PDF is arXiv:2505.08038v1 and prints no DOI, so the DOI-to-title match cannot be checked from the text. The core of the paper is the optimization design (MS-JoCDWM); the learned part (dense Transformer network, MS-JoCDWM-DL) is a complexity-reduction add-on, included because it performs the precoding computation (abstract, p. 1), so the reviewer may confirm. Area 6 over 3 by the tie-break (satellite precoding). Borderline q1: QuaDRiGa generates the large-scale parameters (power, K-factor, angles) of the paper's own Rician model with Gaussian phase errors (pp. 3, 9), and κ is set manually in Fig. 7 (p. 10). Earlier DL precoders [12]–[14] appear only in related work (p. 2).
